Kodiak and Charger disclose Dallas–Laredo freight service with safety drivers

The 435-mile route carries refrigerated and dry freight, with driverless operation contingent on completion of the safety case.

Kodiak AI ↗8 October 2026English editorial summary
StoryImages 1

A newly disclosed freight lane

Kodiak AI and Charger USA announced their collaboration on October 8. Trucks fitted with the Kodiak Driver carry refrigerated and dry freight over a 435-mile route between Dallas and Laredo terminals. The companies say the first delivery occurred on September 8, so the announcement discloses an existing service rather than an October start date.

Safety drivers remain on board

Current operations use a safety driver behind the wheel. The partners intend to transition to driverless service after Kodiak completes its safety case: an evidence-backed argument for safe operation within a defined domain. Under Driver-as-a-Service, customers own and operate trucks equipped with Kodiak’s technology.

Readiness is not a driving success rate

Kodiak reported 96% long-haul readiness at September’s end. That metric measures progress on safety-case claims and evidence, not a 96% driving success rate. Its year-end 2026 long-haul driverless target and potential expansion with Charger remain forward-looking plans.
